1. to be fond of strife, engage in eager rivalry, be contentious , φιλονεικῶν out of contentiousness  or party spirit , (Thucydides); φ. πρός τινα (Lysias Orator):—;with accusative, φ. τὸ ἐμὲ εἶναι τὸν ἀποκρινόμενον to be eager  that I should be the answerer, (Plato Philosophus); τὰ χείρω φ. to be so obstinate as to choose  the worst, (Thucydides) 
2. in good sense, to struggle emulously , φ. περὶ τῶν καλλίστων (Isocrates Orator) (ML)

G9643.d:
1. a muzzle , Lat. capistrum, (Lucian)

3. a kind of cup , used as a dice-box , Lat. fritillus, (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G9644.d: to be heated, inflamed, to fester , φλεγμαίνουσα πόλις, opposite to ὑγιής, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9645.d:
1. transitive to burn, burn up , (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass. to take fire, blaze up , (Iliad by Homer)

6. metaphorically to break forth , of passion, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
7. to shine forth, become famous , (Pindar) (ML)

G9646.d:
1. a vein , (Iliad by Homer), etc.; φλέβα σχάζειν to open a vein , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. a vein  of metal, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9647.d: in plural φλιαί, = σταθμοί, the doorposts, jambs , (Odyssey by Homer); in singular, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G9653.d: purple-red, purple  or crimson , and (generally) red , Lat. puniceus, (Herdotus Historicus):—;attic contracted φοινι-κοῦς, ᾶ, οῦν, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9662.d:
1. a shuddering, shivering , (Plato Philosophus) 
2. shuddering , especially from religious awe, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9664.d: that causes shuddering, horrible , (Euripides):—;neuter φρικῶδες, as adverb horribly , (Euripides):—; adverb -δῶς, Sup., φρικωδέστατα ἔχειν to be in utter horror , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G9665.d:
1. thought, care, heed, attention  bestowed upon a person or thing, with genitive, φροντίδ᾽ ἔχειν τινός (Euripides); ἐν φροντίδι εἶναι περί τινος (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. absolute thought, meditation , (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἐν φροντίδι μοι ἐγένετο [ τὸ πρῆγμα] (Herdotus Historicus); ἐμβῆσαί τινα ἐς φροντίδα to set one a thinking , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;in plural thoughts , αἱ δεύτεραί πως φροντίδες σοφώτεραι (Euripides) 
3. deep thought, care, concern , (Aeschulus Tragicus); οὐ φροντὶς Ἱπποκλείδῃ no matter  to Hippocleides! (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9666.d:
1. a looking out, watch, guard , as a duty, (Herdotus Historicus); φρουρὰν ἄζηλον ὀχήσω shall keep unenviable watch , (Aeschulus Tragicus); φρουρὰ ὄμματος my watchful eye, (Sophocles Tragicus); φρουρᾶς ᾄδειν to sing while on guard , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. a prison , (Plato Philosophus) 
3. of persons, a watch, guard, garrison , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; especially of frontier-posts , which were guarded in Attica by the περίπολοι, (Xenophon Historicus) 
4. at Sparta, a body of men destined for service , φρουρὰν φαίνειν (see. φαίνω A. 1. 5). (ML)

G9668.d:
1. a violent snorting, neighing , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. metaphorically wanton behaviour, insolence , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9670.d:
1. to roast  or fry , (Aristophanes Comicus); ἐρετμοῖσι φρύξουσι they shall cook  with the [wood of] the oars, (Oracle quoted in Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass., πεφρυγμέναι κριθαί roasted  barley, (Thucydides) 
2. of the sun, to parch , Lat. torrere, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G9674.d: to drive from a country, banish , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9675.d:
1. one who flees  from his country, a runaway, fugitive, a banished man, exile, refugee , Lat. exul, profugus, (Herdotus Historicus), attic; φυγάδα ποιεῖν τινα (Xenophon Historicus); κατάγειν φυγάδας to recall them; etc. 
2. of an army, put to flight , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G9676.d:
1. growth, stature , especially fine growth, noble stature , (Homer); Νέστορι εἶδός τε μέγεθός τε φυήν τt ἄγχιστα ἐῴκει he was like Nestor both in shape and size and stature  (or growth) , (Iliad by Homer) 
2. poetry for φύσις, one's natural powers, nature, genius , (Pindar) 
3. the flower  or prime of age , (Pindar) (ML)

G9679.d:
1. the chief of a  φυ_λή, a phylarch , (Herdotus Historicus):—;used to translated the Rom. tribunus , (Plutarch) 
2. at Athens, the commander of the cavalry furnished by each tribe , see. ἵππαρχος. (ML)

G9681.d:
1. to mix  flour or meal so as to make  it into dough, to knead , (Herdotus Historicus); γῆν φυράσειν φόνῳ to make  earth into a  bloody paste , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;Pass., οἴνῳ καὶ ἐλαίῳ πεφυραμένα ἄλφιτα (Thucydides) 
2. metaphorically, μαλακὴν φωνὴν φυράσασθαι to make up  a soft voice, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9683.d:
1. to mix  something dry with  something wet , mostly with a sense of mixing so as to soil  or defile , δάκρυσιν εἵματ᾽ ἔφυρον they wetted, sullied  their garments with tears, (Iliad by Homer); also with genitive, χείλεα φύρσω αἵματος (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass., δάκρυσι πεφυρμένη (Iliad by Homer); αἵματι οἶκος ἐφύρθη (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. of dry things, κόνει φύρουσα κάρα (Euripides); γαίαι πεφύρσεσθαι κόμαν to be doomed to have  one's hair defiled  with earth, (Pindar) 
3. metaphorically to mingle together, confuse , ἔφυρον εἰκῆ πάντα they mixed  all things up together, did all at random, (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.:—;Pass. to be mixed up , ἐκ πεφυρμένου καὶ θηριώδους from a confused  and savage state, (Euripides) 
4. in Pass. also to mix with others, have dealings with  him, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9684.d:
1. transitive to puff  or blow up, distend , (Aristophanes Comicus); of bag-pipers, (Aristophanes Comicus); φ. τὰς γνάθους to puff  them out , (Demosthenes Orator):—;Pass. to be inflated , ἡ γαστὴρ ἐπεφύσητό μοι (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. metaphorically to puff  one up, make  him vain , and so to cheat , (Demosthenes Orator):—;Pass. to be puffed up , ἐπί τινι at a thing, (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. to blow up, kindle  a fire: but also 
4. to blow out, extinguish , τὴν λαμπάδα (Aristophanes Comicus) 
5. to blow out, spurt out , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
6. to blow  a wind-instrument, (Euripides) (ML)

G9685.d: an instrument for blowing, blowpipe  or tube , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9687.d:
1. that which has grown, a plant, tree , (Iliad by Homer), etc. 
2. generally a creature , of men, (Euripides) 
3. like ἔρνος, of men, a descendant, child , (Euripides) (ML)

G9688.d:
1. to search after a thief  or theft, search a house , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. in Pass. to be detected , (Demosthenes Orator); with participle, κλέπτης ὢν φωρᾶσθαι (Demosthenes Orator); so, κακὸς [ ὢν] ἐφωράθη φίλοις (Euripides):—;also of things, ἀργύριον ἐφωράθη ἐξαγόμενον money was discovered  to be in course of exportation, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9693.d:
1. a small stone, pebble , in plural, (Lucian), etc. 
2. as collect. in singular, gravel, rubble , used in building, (Thucydides); so also in plural, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9694.d:
1. a smith's shop, forge, smithy , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. = χαλκίον, a copper, caldron , (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. a metal reflector  in a lamp, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9695.d: of copper  or bronze, brasen , (Homer); χαλκήιος δόμος, = χαλκεῖον, a forge , (Odyssey by Homer); χάλκειον γένος, of the Age of brass , (Hesiod) (ML)

G9696.d:
1. to make of copper  or (generally) of metal, to forge , (Iliad by Homer), etc.:—;Mid. to forge for oneself , (Theognis Elegiacus):—;Pass. to be wrought  or forged , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. absolute to be a smith, work as a smith, ply the hammer , (Aristophanes Comicus); τὸ χαλκεύειν the smith's art , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9697.d: the chameleon , a kind of lizard known for changing its colour, (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G9698.d:
1. chaos , the first stateof the universe, (Hesiod), etc. 
2. infinite space, the expanse , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
3. the nether abyss, infinite darkness , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9699.d: perhaps a yellowish bird dwelling in clefts the curlew , (Aristophanes Comicus): χαραδριοῦ βίον ζῆν, of a glutton, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9701.d: to fence by a palisade, fortify , (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G9703.d:
1. to make sharp  or pointed, sharpen, whet , (Hesiod) 
2. to furnish with notches  or teeth , like a saw, (Aristotle Philosopher):—;Pass., σκύταλον κεχ. ὄζοις a staff jagged  or rugged  with branches, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus): metaphorically, [ ὄμμα] ἠλεμάτοις ἀκτῖσι χαράσσεται sparkles  with false lights, of the effect produced by painting the eye-lids, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
3. metaphorically in Pass., κεχαραγμένος τινί exasperated at  any one, (Herdotus Historicus); κείνῳ τόδε μὴ χαράσσου be not angry at  him for  this, (Euripides) 
4. to cut into furrows, cut, scratch , (Pindar):—;Pass., κέκοπται καὶ χαράσσεται πέδον (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
5. to engrave, inscribe , [Refs 3rd c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9704.d:
1. a joy , (Euripides); plural joys, delights , (Euripides) 
2. = χάρμα II, joy, delight , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G9710.d:
1. of  or in winter, of  or in winter-time , opposite to θερινός, χ. τροπαί (see. τροπή 1), (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; τὴν χ. (i.e. ὥρην); during the winter season , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. wintry , (Thucydides); see. χειμέριος. (ML)

G9712.d:
1. a voting  or electing by show of hands , (Thucydides) 
2. a vote , Lat. suffragium, in plural, (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G9713.d:
1. to bring into hand, to manage, master, subdue , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. mostly in Mid., to conquer, overpower, subdue , (Herdotus Historicus); so, τήνδ᾽ ἐχειρούμην ἄγραν became master of  this booty, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
3. without any sense of violence, to master, subdue , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. 
4. χειροῦμαι is also Pass. to be subdued , [variant datesTragica Adespota; future χειρωθήσομαι (Demosthenes Orator); aor1 ἐχειρώθην (Herdotus Historicus); perfect κεχείρωμαι (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9714.d:
1. the swallow , (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—; the twittering of the swallow was proverbially used of barbarous tongues by the Greeks, (Aeschulus Tragicus); χελιδόνων μουσεῖα (see. μουσεῖον);  proverbs also, μία χελιδὼν ἔαρ οὐ ποιεῖ (Aristotle Philosopher) 
2. the frog in a horse's foot , so called from its being forked like the swallow's tail , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9715.d:
1. a tortoise , (Homeric Hymns); prov. of insensibility, ἰὼ χελῶναι μακάριαι τοῦ δέρματος oh ye tortoises , happy in your thick skins! (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. like Roman testudo, a pent-house formed of shields overlapping each other like the scales on a tortoise's back , used by storming parties in approaching a city's walls: then, generally, a pent-house  for protecting besiegers, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9718.d: on  or of dry land , ὄρνιθες χ. land- birds, opposite to λιμναῖοι, (Herdotus Historicus); χ. κροκόδειλος a lizard, (Herdotus Historicus):—;also of landsmen , as opposite to seamen, (Euripides); κῦμα χερσαῖον στρατοῦ, an army, opposite to a fleet, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9719.d:
1. dry land, land , ἐπὶ χέρσου, opposite to ἐν πόντῳ, (Odyssey by Homer); κύματα κυλινδόμενα προτὶ χέρσον (Odyssey by Homer); κῦμα χέρσῳ ῥηγνύμενον (Iliad by Homer); χέρσῳ on  or by land , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. as adjective, χέρσος, ον, dry, firm , of land, (Herdotus Historicus); ἐν κονίᾳ χέρσῳ, opposite to πόντῳ, (Pindar) 
3. dry, hard, barren , (Herdotus Historicus); χ. λιμήν a harbour left dry , [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
4. metaphorically barren, without children , of women, (Sophocles Tragicus): with genitive barren of , πυρὰ χέρσος ἀγλαϊσμάτων (Euripides) 
Prob. from same Root as ξηρός. (ML)

G9721.d:
1. Radic. sense, to pour : 
2. properly of liquids, to pour out, pour , (Homer), etc.; Zeus χέει ὕδωρ, i. e. he makes it rain, (Iliad by Homer); χέει χιόνα βορέας (Euripides); absolute, χέει it snows , (Iliad by Homer):—;Mid. to pour for oneself , especially of drink-offerings, χοὰς χεόμην νεκύεσσι (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—;Pass., χέονται κρῆναι they gush forth , (Euripides); χυθέντος ποτοῦ ἐς γῆν (Sophocles Tragicus) 
3. χ. δάκρυα to shed  tears, (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass., of tears, to pour  or gush forth , (Homer); so of blood, to be shed , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
4. in Pass. to become liquid, melt, thaw , (Xenophon Historicus) 
5. of solids, to shed, scatter , φύλλα (Iliad by Homer); πτερά (Odyssey by Homer); χ. κόνιν κὰκ κεφαλῆς (Homer); χ. καλάμην χθονί, of a mower or reaper (see. καλάμη), (Iliad by Homer) 
6. like χώννυμι, to throw out  earth, so as to form a mound, σῆμα, τύμβον χ. (Homer) 
7. χ. δοῦρα to pour  or shower  spears, (Iliad by Homer); Mid., βέλεα χέοντο they showered their  arrows, (Iliad by Homer) 
8. to let fall  or drop , ἡνία (Iliad by Homer); so, χέειν κρόκου βαφὰς (see. βαφή II) (Aeschulus Tragicus); but, καρπὸν χ., of trees, to produce  fruit abundantly , (Odyssey by Homer) 
9. in Pass. to be thrown  or heaped up together , (Homer) 
10. in Pass. also of living beings, to pour  or stream in a dense mass  or throng , (Homer) 
11. metaphorically of sounds, to pour forth , φωνήν, αὐδήν (Odyssey by Homer); φθόγγον (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
12. of things that obscure the sight, κατ᾽ ὀφθαλμῶν χέεν ἀχλύν shed  a dark cloud over the eyes, (Iliad by Homer); πολλὴν ἠέρα χεῦε shed  a mist abroad, (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass., ἀμφὶ δέ οἱ θάνατος χύτο was shed  around him, (Iliad by Homer); νόσος κέχυται (Sophocles Tragicus); φρὶξ ἐπὶ πόντον ἐχεύατο (Mid. in passive sense), (Iliad by Homer) 
13. of persons, ἀμφ᾽ αὐτῶι χυμένη throwing herself  around him, (Homer): so in Mid., ἀμφὶ υἱὸν ἐχεύατο πήχεε (Iliad by Homer) 
14. perfect passive κέχυμαι, to be wholly engaged in , Δᾶλος, ἐν ἇι κέχυμαι (Pindar) (ML)

G9722.d:
1. a horse's hoof , (Hesiod):—;also, a cloven hoof , (Euripides) 
2. in plural, of the talons  of a bird, [variant datesTragica Adespota; of a wolf's claws , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 
3. a sea-bank, breakwater , formed of stones laid at the base of a sea-wall, to break the force of the waves (so called because it projected like a hoof) , Lat. crepido, (Thucydides) 
4. the spur of a mountain  or ridge of rocks  answering a like purpose, (Thucydides) 
5. a cloven implement , such as a netting-needle;—;  compare χηλεύω. (ML)

G9725.d:
1. intransitive to be bereaved  of a person or thing, with genitive, (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. absolute to be bereaved of a husband, to be widowed, live in widowhood , (Demosthenes Orator), etc.;—;of a man, to be a widower , (Plutarch); so, χηρεύσει λέχος (Euripides) 
3. to live in solitude , of an exile, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
4. transitive to bereave , (Euripides) (ML)

G9726.d: of yesterday , τὸ χθιζὸν χρεῖος their yesterday's  debt, (Iliad by Homer); ὁ χθ. πόνος yesterday's  labour, (Herdotus Historicus); in adverbial sense, with Verbs, χθιζὸς ἔβη he went yesterday , (Iliad by Homer); χθ. ἤλυθες (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—;neuter χθιζόν as adverb = χθές, (Homer); so plural χθιζά, see. πρώιζος. (ML)

G9727.d:
1. the earth, ground , (Homer); χθόνα δῦναι to go beneath the earth , i. e. to die, (Iliad by Homer); κατὰ χθονὸς κρύπτειν τινά (Sophocles Tragicus); κούφα σοι χθὼν ἐπάνω πέσοι (Euripides) 
2. of the nether world , οἱ ὑπὸ χθονός, i. e. those in the shades below , Lat. inferi, (Aeschulus Tragicus); κατὰ χθονὸς θεαί, i. e. the Erinyes, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
3. earth , i. e. the whole earth, the world , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
4. Earth , as a goddess, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
5. a particular land  or country , of Ithaca, (Odyssey by Homer); of Libya, (Pindar); χθὼν Ἀσιᾶτις, Δωρίς, Ἀργεία, Ἑλλάς, Ἰδαία, etc., [variant datesTragica Adespota (ML)

G9728.d: unripe wheaten groats , as ἄλφιτα are barley-groats, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9729.d:
1. the office  or post  of χιλίαρχος, (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. the office of the tribuni militares , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9732.d:
1. a she-goat , Lat. capra, (Iliad by Homer), attic 
2. Χίμαιρα, ἡ, Chimaera , a firespouting-monster, with lion's head, serpent's tail, and goat's body, killed by Bellerophon, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G9733.d:
1. a he-goat , Lat. caper, = τράγος, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. also feminine = χίμαιρα, [Refs 3rd c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9735.d:

derivation uncertain (ML)

G9741.d:
1. any light porous substance , ἁλὸς χνόος the foam that gathers at the edge  of the sea, (Odyssey by Homer); πωλικὸς χν. horse's foam , [variant datesAnthology Palantina

G9744.d:

G9746.d:
1. gut-string, the string  of a lyre, Lat. chorda, (Odyssey by Homer)

G9748.d:

G9751.d: a being fed, feasting , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9753.d: a coos, a measurement of liquid (Lev.19.36)
